query: I am interested in high-entropy alloys for extreme temperature applications. How can we predict melting properties such as the melting temperature, entropy of fusion, and heat capacity for multi-component systems where experimental data is sparse or unreliable due to high melting points? I am looking for a hypothesis on a computational methodology that balances accuracy with the need to screen vast compositional spaces, along with prior evidence on why standard approaches struggle in this regime and what a valid boundary condition for such a method would be.

generation.hypothesis: A hybrid computational framework combining high-throughput CALPHAD screening with machine learning models trained on Holder means of elemental properties and structural descriptors can accurately predict melting temperatures and entropy of fusion for refractory high-entropy alloys, overcoming the limitations of standard molecular dynamics with Lennard-Jones potentials and the scarcity of experimental data at extreme temperatures.
generation.material_initial_state: Multi-component refractory high-entropy alloys (e.g., Nb-Mo-Ta-W-V systems) with disordered BCC or FCC solid solution matrices, where experimental melting data is sparse or unreliable due to melting points exceeding 2000 °C.
generation.intervention: Implement a two-stage computational workflow: (1) Use high-throughput CALPHAD to screen thousands of compositions for phase stability and approximate melting ranges, followed by (2) applying a Machine Learning model utilizing Holder means of elemental properties (group numbers, atomic radii, electronegativity) and structural properties (cohesive energy, density) to predict specific melting thermodynamics (Tm, ΔS_fus, C_p).
generation.conditions: Compositional space restricted to systems where thermodynamic databases are sufficiently populated (e.g., Al < 25 at.% or specific refractory sets), operating at temperatures approaching the melting point (Tm) where lattice disorder becomes dominant, and avoiding systems with very large heats of formation (e.g., oxides) where high-entropy theory fails.
generation.structural_mediator: The disordered solid solution matrix where atomic size mismatch and lattice distortion drive the entropy of fusion, and where the transition from stacking fault formation to lattice disorder occurs near the melting point.
generation.mechanism: Standard Molecular Dynamics (MD) with Lennard-Jones potentials fails to capture the complex multi-body interactions in HEAs, leading to unreliable predictions. The proposed hybrid method bypasses this by using CALPHAD for phase fraction screening (validating phase stability) and ML models trained on Holder means to extrapolate thermodynamic properties from known elemental and structural trends, effectively capturing the 'high-entropy' contribution to melting without requiring explicit atomistic simulation of the liquid phase.
generation.predicted_outcome: The hybrid method will identify candidate alloys with Tm > 1250 °C and specific phase fractions (e.g., L2_1 or BCC) with prediction errors for melting properties significantly lower (<10%) than those obtained from pure MD or conventional CALPHAD without high-throughput automation, enabling the screening of vast compositional spaces where experimental data is unavailable.
generation.baseline: Conventional CALPHAD calculations without high-throughput automation, trial-and-error experimental methods, and Molecular Dynamics simulations using only Lennard-Jones potentials which have been shown to be unreliable for multi-component systems.
generation.boundary: The method is valid only for systems where the thermodynamic databases are of sufficient quality (as accuracy depends on database parameters) and excludes systems with very large heats of formation (like oxides) where high-entropy theory does not apply. It is also limited to composition ranges where the database parameters are optimized (e.g., Al < 25 at.% in Al-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ti systems).
generation.uncertainty: High uncertainty exists regarding the accuracy of the thermodynamic databases for less studied systems or extreme temperatures, as the quality of predictions is directly dependent on the available experimental data used to optimize model parameters. Additionally, the ML model's training on ordered compounds may introduce errors when applied to disordered HEAs due to lattice distortion effects not fully captured in the training set.

falsification_experiment.design: Select a refractory HEA system (e.g., NbMoTaWV) with no existing experimental melting data. Run the proposed hybrid workflow (CALPHAD + ML) to predict Tm and ΔS_fus. Then, synthesize the alloy using a high-temperature method capable of reaching the predicted melting point (e.g., SLM or specialized arc melting) and measure the actual melting temperature and heat capacity using differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) or laser flash analysis.
measurements: Entropy of fusion (ΔS_fus) derived from heat capacity integration
Phase fractions at Tm via in-situ XRD
Comparison of predicted vs. measured values
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if the predicted melting temperature deviates from the experimental value by more than 15% or if the predicted entropy of fusion deviates by more than 20%, indicating that the ML model trained on Holder means and CALPHAD screening cannot accurately capture the thermodynamics of the specific refractory system under extreme conditions.

Statement: The accuracy of thermodynamic predictions is highly dependent on the quality of the databases, which may be incomplete or inaccurate for less studied systems or high temperatures.. System: CrMnFeCoNi High-Entropy Alloy. Lever: database quality. Quote: "Furthermore, the accuracy of all these properties depends highly on the quality of the databases that, in turn, ultimately rely on the available experimental data for optimizing the model parameters and validation."

Mechanism with scope. Mechanism: Machine learning models using Holder means of elemental properties (group numbers, atomic radii, electronegativity) and structural properties (cohesive energy, density) can predict shear and bulk moduli for disordered HEAs with good accuracy.. System: NbTaTiV BCC refractory high-entropy alloy. Conditions: Room temperature (prediction based on training data from ordered compounds). Evidence: simulated. Observation: The ML model predicted a shear modulus of 36.6 GPa and bulk modulus of 146.3 GPa, with relative errors of 2.5% and 6% compared to experimental values.. Scope limits: The model was trained on ordered compounds from the Materials Project database, not disordered alloys; the lattice distortion effect in HEAs might cause less accurate results, though agreement was good.. Alternatives: First-principles calculations (DFT) which showed larger deviations (-15.9% to -16.6% for Young's and shear moduli).. Gap and lever. Type: limitation. Statement: The lack of HEA phase diagrams limits the availability of thermodynamic data for predicting phase formation.. System: High entropy alloys (HEA). Lever: thermodynamic data availability or phase diagram construction. Quote: "Although a lack of HEA phase diagrams limit the availability of thermodynamic data, some thermodynamic properties, such as atomic size, melting point, mixing entropy, mixing enthalpy, and valence electron concentration, can be used as criteria to predict the phase formation in the HEA system."

Mechanism with scope. Mechanism: The CALPHAD-based high-throughput computational method can efficiently screen thousands of compositions to identify alloys with specific phase fractions (BCC and L2 1) and melting temperatures suitable for high-temperature applications.. System: Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti quinary system. Conditions: Computational screening at various temperatures (Tm, 0.8Tm, 0.5Tm); step size of 5 at.%. Evidence: simulated. Observation: The method screened 3246 alloys, identifying 8 candidates that met criteria for Tm > 1250 °C and specific L2 1 volume fractions at operating temperatures.. Scope limits: Valid in the composition range of Al < 25 at.% and Mn > 15 at.% with unchanged contents of other elements; accuracy depends on the thermodynamic database.. Alternatives: Trial-and-error experimental method; conventional CALPHAD calculations without high-throughput automation.. Quote: "Through the high-throughput screening, precipitation-strengthened lightweight high-entropy alloys are discovered from thousands of initial compositions"
